paper.title: Selective targeting of lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2) suppresses hepatic fibrosis progression and accelerates its reversal

causal_target.important_boundary: crosslinking and matrix stability were measured biochemically and morphologically; tissue elastic modulus was not the primary intervention readout

delayed_progression_arm.injury_model: TAA-induced pan-lobular liver fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice
delayed_progression_arm.pre_existing_state: after 6 weeks of TAA, significant pericentral fibrosis with bridging was already established
delayed_progression_arm.treatment_window: weeks 7-12 of continued TAA fibrosis induction

result.overall_collagen_deposition: partly reduced relative to start-of-treatment controls
result.crosslinked_collagen: significantly reduced; delayed treatment inhibited further stabilization of the insoluble collagen fraction

reversal_arm.setup: 6 weeks TAA to establish fibrosis, then TAA withdrawn and mice allowed to recover with AB0023, control antibody or vehicle
reversal_arm.result: anti-LOXL2 accelerated disruption, widening and splitting of fibrotic septa and reduced connective-tissue burden during early recovery
reversal_arm.interpretation: blocking late collagen crosslink stabilization accelerates remodeling of already-established fibrotic architecture

timing_specificity.late_window: effective when started after 6 weeks of established fibrosis
timing_specificity.early_window: the same anti-LOXL2 strategy was reported as ineffective when applied during an earlier weeks 3-8 progression window
timing_specificity.meaning: the causal contribution of LOXL2-mediated matrix stabilization is phase-dependent rather than monotonic across the full injury course

cell_state_context.activated_HSC: LOXL2 localized in fibrotic septa in a distribution similar to collagen I and alpha-SMA-positive activated hepatic stellate cells
cell_state_context.HPC: LOXL2 also influenced hepatic progenitor lineage commitment independently of collagen crosslinking
cell_state_context.confound: the antibody can therefore affect both extracellular matrix stabilization and cell-autonomous/paracrine LOXL2 biology; it is not a pure mechanics-only perturbation

gate_verdict.why: This is a clean delayed intervention against an established matrix-stabilization mechanism, but does not provide a matched point-level elastic-modulus trajectory or a primary organ-function endpoint.

next_killer_measurement: repeat delayed LOXL2/crosslink intervention with longitudinal AFM/rheology of liver stiffness, same-state activated-HSC trajectories, matrix crosslink fractions and organ-function/regeneration endpoints
